turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip said he would call Estella at the door, but before he could move, Miss Havisham’s voice stopped him.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham said to Pip, holding up a hand to pause him, that Estella would be there shortly. She added, in a tone that hinted at deeper motives, that he should observe Estella well, for she had a purpose in mind.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip nodded, feeling a mix of curiosity and trepidation. He would observe Estella well, as Miss Havisham had said, but the task felt daunting and a bit unnerving.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip with a calculating gaze, her eyes glinting in the dim light. She told him, in a voice that hinted at secrets and shadows, that Estella was a creature of her making, and that Pip should note how she wielded her influence.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a chill run down his spine at Miss Havisham’s words, and he nodded again, more out of a sense of duty than understanding, as he waited for Estella to appear.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham leaned back, her gaze fixed on the door through which Estella would soon appear, and mused, with a hint of a twisted smile, that Pip would soon see the world through her eyes.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a knot in his stomach, he told Miss Havisham, and he would do as she asked, though he did not quite understand why.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham nodded, her expression unreadable, and instructed Pip to be observant, as there were lessons to be learned from Estella’s interactions.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a shiver of unease, he told Miss Havisham, and he would try to be observant as she suggested, though he did not know what lessons there were to learn.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes gleamed with a peculiar light as she stared at Pip, her voice barely above a whisper, telling him that in time, he would understand the lessons she sought to impart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt the weight of Miss Havisham's gaze and told her that he would try to understand, though it seemed a daunting task.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes darkened as she looked at Pip, her voice low and commanding. She told him that patience was a virtue and that understanding would come, though it might not be a comforting journey.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a knot in his stomach, he told Miss Havisham, and though he would try to be patient, the lessons she spoke of seemed to be far beyond his understanding.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham sighed heavily, her eyes lingering on Pip with a mixture of curiosity and disdain. She told him that understanding life’s lessons was never easy, especially when those lessons were bitter and twisted like the paths she herself had trodden.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a shiver run down his spine, he told Miss Havisham, and though he would try to be patient, the lessons she spoke of seemed to be far beyond his understanding.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes glinted as she looked at Pip, her voice icy yet captivating. She told him that the world was full of lessons, some bitter and twisted, but all necessary for growth and understanding.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a cold sweat break out on his brow, he told Miss Havisham, and though he would try to be patient, the lessons she spoke of seemed to be far beyond his understanding.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes flickered with a strange mixture of pity and mockery, as she gazed at Pip. She told him that patience was a virtue, but only for those who understood the true nature of the world’s games.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt his heart sinking, he told Miss Havisham, and though he would try to be patient, the lessons she spoke of seemed to be far beyond his understanding.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes fell upon Pip's quivering form, her gaze sharpening with a mix of disdain and a peculiar sort of amusement. She informed him that the world was a vast stage, and one could learn much by watching the players, even if they did not always understand the script.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
